s: the Doom is tasted by the guilty (as painful punishment)
q: Lo! (now) verily ye taste the painful doom -

l: Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: creation is created from plastic clay (human creation)
q: Lo! We created them of plastic clay.

l: Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: Allah is lord of the earth
q: Lord of the heavens and of the earth and all that is between them, and Lord of the sun's risings.

l: Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: revelation and remembrance is a reminder (read for guidance)
q: And those who read (the Word) for a reminder,

l: Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: the tree of Zaqqum is a torment (appointed for wrong-doers)

l: Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: the tree of Zaqqum grows in hell (in its heart)

l: Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)

s: monotheism is stated as There is no Allah save Allah (the rejected declaration of the idolaters)

s: judgment and accountability is required of the guilty (they must answer for their deeds)
q: And stop them, for they must be questioned.

s: punishment is requital for deeds (according to what people did)

s: salvation and reward are for the good (as Allah's recompense)

s: Allah is lord of the men of old (through their forefathers)
q: Allah, your Lord and Lord of your forefathers?

s: Allah is best of creators
q: Will ye cry unto Baal and forsake the Best of creators,

s: Allah is glorified above false_attributes
q: Glorified be Allah from that which they attribute (unto Him),

l: Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: This unit concerns Allah's revelation, creation, judgment, mercy, and punishment, as well as the responses of humanity, disbelievers, Iblis, and earlier peoples. Allah describes the preservation of the Reminder, the creation of humanity and the jinn, the angels' prostration before the created mortal, and Iblis's expulsion and promise to mislead. The messengers visit Abraham with the annunciation of a wise boy and are sent to destroy the sinful people of Lot while rescuing Lot's family. The unit recounts the destruction of the dwellers in the wood and Al-Hijr, and instructs Muhammad to proclaim the revelation, worship Allah, and endure until the Inevitable comes.

l: Allah, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Allah reveals and guards the Reminder, creates the heavens, earth, humanity, and the jinn, gives life and death, and knows the eager and the laggards. Allah promises mercy to devoted slaves and punishment for the guilty, and will gather all together.

l: Muhammad, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Muhammad is told to proclaim what he is commanded, withdraw from the idolaters, praise Allah, prostrate, and serve his Lord until the Inevitable comes. Allah tells him not to grieve over worldly things and promises to defend him from scoffers.

l: Iblis, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Iblis refuses to prostrate to the mortal created from potter's clay and is expelled and cursed until the Day of Judgment. He asks for reprieve and declares that he will adorn error and mislead humanity, except Allah's perfectly devoted slaves.

l: Abraham, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Abraham receives messengers who bring him good tidings of a boy possessing wisdom. He rejects despair of his Lord's mercy and asks the messengers about their mission.

l: Lot, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Lot receives the messengers and is told to travel with his household by night without turning around. His wife is decreed to remain behind while the rest of his family is delivered.

l: angels, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: The angels prostrate together before the mortal Allah creates, except Iblis. Messengers come to Abraham with good tidings and are sent against a guilty people while rescuing Lot's family.

l: humanity, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Humanity is created from potter's clay of black mud altered, while the jinn are created from essential fire. People are given livelihoods, but Iblis seeks to mislead them except for Allah's devoted slaves.

l: disbelievers, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Disbelievers mock the messenger, call him a madman, demand angels, and reject the Reminder. They would explain even an opened gate of heaven as faulty sight or sorcery.

l: messengers, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Messengers were sent among earlier peoples, but those peoples mocked them. The messengers visiting Abraham bring truth and good tidings, and they are sent to a guilty folk while sparing Lot's family.

l: the dwellers in Al-Hijr, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: The dwellers in Al-Hijr deny the messengers and turn away from the revelations. Although they hew secure dwellings from the hills, the Awful Cry overtakes them in the morning and their gains do not benefit them.

l: Al-Hijr, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Al-Hijr is associated with people who deny the messengers and are destroyed by the Awful Cry. It is presented as a sign for believers and as lying upon a road still uneffaced.

l: heaven, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Allah sets mansions of the stars in heaven and beautifies it for beholders. Heaven is guarded from every outcast devil, except one who steals hearing and is pursued by a clear flame.

l: earth, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Allah spreads out the earth, places firm hills in it, causes seemly things to grow, and provides livelihoods. Iblis says he will adorn the path of error for humanity in the earth.

l: hell, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Hell is the promised place for those who follow Iblis. It has seven gates, each with an appointed portion.

l: gardens, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Those who ward off evil are in gardens and watersprings. They enter in peace and security, with rancour removed from their breasts, and they are not expelled or troubled by toil.

l: the Scripture, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: The opening verses identify the Scripture and a plain Reading as signs of revelation.

l: the Reminder, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Allah reveals the Reminder and declares that He guards it. The guilty do not believe in it even though the example of earlier peoples has gone before.

l: the Qur'an, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Muhammad is given seven of the oft-repeated verses and the great Qur'an. Some people break the Qur'an into parts and will be questioned about what they did.

l: revelation, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Revelation is guarded by Allah and is sent in appointed measure. The unit commands Muhammad to proclaim what has been revealed and warns that those who divide it will be questioned.

l: creation of humanity, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Humanity is created from potter's clay of black mud altered. Allah then makes the mortal and breathes into him of His Spirit.

l: the prostration before Adam, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: The angels fall down prostrating together before the mortal Allah creates. Iblis refuses to join them because he will not prostrate to a mortal made from potter's clay.

l: Iblis's expulsion, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: After refusing the prostration, Iblis is ordered to go forth and is declared outcast, with the curse upon him until the Day of Judgment.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: The curse upon Iblis lasts until the Day of Judgment. Allah will gather all together, and Iblis and the guilty will face their appointed consequences.

l: resurrection, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Iblis asks to be reprieved until the day when people are raised, and Allah grants reprieve until the appointed time.

l: destruction of the sinful peoples, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Allah destroys townships according to known decrees and destroys sinful peoples who reject the messengers. The people of Lot, the dwellers in the wood, and the dwellers in Al-Hijr are among those whose destruction is described.

l: the angels' visit to Abraham, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Messengers visit Abraham and greet him with peace, but he fears them. They reassure him and announce a boy possessing wisdom before explaining that they have been sent to a guilty folk.

l: the annunciation of Isaac, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Abraham receives good tidings of a boy possessing wisdom despite his old age. The messengers tell him that the good tidings are true and that he should not despair.

l: the mission against Lot's people, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: The messengers are sent to a guilty folk and tell Lot that they bring the truth concerning what the people dispute. They instruct Lot to travel by night with his household.

l: the angels' rescue of Lot's family, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: The messengers promise to deliver Lot's family, except his wife, whom Allah decrees to remain behind. Lot is instructed not to let anyone turn around while leaving.

l: the destruction at sunrise, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: The people of the city come rejoicing, but the Awful Cry overtakes them at sunrise. Allah utterly confounds them and rains stones of heated clay upon them.

l: divine creation, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Allah creates the heavens, earth, and everything between them with truth. He creates humanity from clay, the jinn from essential fire, and gives life and death.

l: mercy and forgiveness, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Allah describes Himself as the Forgiving and the Merciful. Abraham says that only those who are astray despair of the mercy of their Lord.

l: divine punishment, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Allah warns that His doom is dolorous and appoints hell for those who follow Iblis. He destroys rejecting peoples through the Awful Cry and stones of heated clay.

l: guidance and error, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Iblis promises to adorn the path of error and mislead humanity, but he has no power over Allah's slaves except the froward who follow him. Allah identifies a right course as incumbent upon Him.

l: worship, Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr), Surah 15: The Rock (Al-Hijr)
s: Muhammad is instructed to hymn the praise of his Lord, make prostration, and serve his Lord until the Inevitable comes. The unit also describes the devoted slaves whom Iblis cannot control.

l: Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl) concerns Allah’s signs, commands, revelation, and judgment, and calls mankind to worship Him alone, give thanks, and act justly. It describes the creation and service of the heavens, the earth, water, the sea, cattle, the bee, and other creatures as signs for those who reflect. It contrasts those who believe and do good with those who disbelieve, the idolaters, and the proud, describing their respective rewards and punishments in the Hereafter. Muhammad is instructed to convey the message, call with wisdom, endure patiently, and follow the religion of Abraham.

l: Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: It presents Allah’s signs in creation, His revelation and commands, the duties of mankind, and the consequences awaiting those who believe or disbelieve.

l: Allah, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: Allah creates, provides, guides, judges, forgives, and sends revelation. He commands worship of Him alone, justice, kindness, fulfillment of covenants, patience, and gratitude.

l: Muhammad, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: Muhammad receives the Remembrance and is instructed to explain the revelation, call to Allah’s way with wisdom, endure patiently, and not grieve over those who reject the message.

l: Abraham, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: Abraham is described as obedient to Allah, upright, thankful for His bounties, chosen and guided, and not an idolater. Muhammad is instructed to follow his religion.

l: the angels, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: The angels descend with the Spirit of Allah’s command and cause the good and the wrongdoers to die. They prostrate to Allah, fear their Lord, and do what they are commanded.

l: the Spirit, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: The Spirit delivers revelation from Muhammad’s Lord with truth, confirming believers and serving as guidance and good tidings for those who surrender to Allah.

l: mankind, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: Mankind is created from a drop of fluid and given hearing, sight, and hearts. Mankind receives provision and signs from Allah but is warned against pride, idolatry, false claims, and ingratitude.

l: the heavens, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: The heavens are created with truth and belong to Allah. What is in them is subject to Allah, and the unseen of the heavens and the earth belongs to Him.

l: the earth, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: The earth is created with truth and contains firm hills, streams, roads, landmarks, varied things, and provision. Allah revives it with water after its death.

l: the cattle, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: The cattle provide warm clothing, uses, food, beauty, transport, and milk. Their wool, fur, hair, and hides provide furnishings, shelter, and comfort.

l: water, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: Allah sends water down from the sky, giving mankind drink and causing trees, crops, olives, dates, grapes, and other fruits to grow. Water also revives the earth after its death.

l: the sea, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: The sea is constrained for mankind’s service, providing fresh meat and ornaments. Ships travel through it so mankind may seek Allah’s bounty and give thanks.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: The Hereafter is the greater reward for those who are steadfast and do good. Those who disbelieve, mislead others, or choose worldly life over it face loss and punishment.

l: the Fire, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: The Fire is the fate of those who assign to Allah what they dislike and invent lies against Him. Those who enter it dwell there in painful punishment.

l: Gardens of Eden, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: Gardens of Eden are promised to those who ward off evil. They enter them with rivers flowing beneath and receive whatever they wish.

l: those who believe, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: Those who believe and put their trust in Allah are protected from the devil. Whoever does right, male or female, while believing, receives a good life and a recompense according to the best of their deeds.

l: those who disbelieve, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: Those who disbelieve reject Allah’s revelations, deny the Hereafter, and oppose guidance. They face humiliation, sealed hearts and senses, painful doom, the Fire, and loss in the Hereafter.

l: the idolaters, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: The idolaters worship beside Allah, assign partners and daughters to Him, and claim that Allah willed their idolatry. They are warned that their inventions will fail and that they will face punishment.

l: the messengers, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: The messengers are sent to every nation to proclaim service to Allah and avoidance of false gods. Their duty is plain conveyance of the message.

l: the Remembrance, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: The Remembrance is revealed to Muhammad so that he may explain to mankind what has been revealed and so that they may reflect.

l: the Scripture, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: The Scripture is revealed to Muhammad as an exposition of all things, guidance, mercy, and good tidings for those who surrender to Allah.

l: the Qur'an, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: The Qur'an is to be recited after seeking refuge in Allah from the outcast Satan. Its revelation is delivered by the holy Spirit with truth.

l: the devil, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: The devil makes the deeds of those before Muhammad seem fair and is the patron of those who follow him. He has no power over those who believe and trust in their Lord, but has power over those who befriend him and assign partners to Allah.

l: the bee, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: The bee receives inspiration to make its habitations in hills, trees, and structures people build, and to eat fruits while following its Lord’s ways. From its belly comes a drink of varied hues containing healing for mankind.

l: the revelation, Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl), Surah 16: The Bee (An-Nahl)
s: Revelation is sent by Allah, and one revelation may be put in place of another according to what Allah knows. The revelation confirms believers and provides guidance and good tidings for those who surrender.

l: The Believers (Al-Muminoon), The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: The unit describes the qualities and reward of the believers, including humility in prayer, avoidance of vain talk, charity, modesty, keeping pledges, and attentiveness to prayer. It recounts Allah's creation of man, provision of water, gardens, cattle, and ships, and the missions and rejection of Noah, Moses, Aaron, and other messengers. It contrasts the believers with disbelievers who deny resurrection, reject the revelations, divide the religion into sects, and face punishment, hell, and the fire. It affirms Allah's oneness, the coming Day of Resurrection, the weighing of deeds, and the triumph of steadfast slaves.

l: Allah, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Allah creates, provides, gives life and death, and will gather people to Him. He has no son or partner, is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Tremendous Throne, and is exalted above what people allege.

l: the believers, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: The believers are humble in prayer, shun vain conversation, pay the poor-due, guard their modesty, keep pledges and covenants, and heed their prayers. They will inherit paradise and abide there.

l: paradise, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Paradise is inherited by the successful believers, who will abide there.

l: man, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Man is created from a product of wet earth and develops from a drop into a clot, a lump, bones, flesh, and another creation. Man then dies and is raised again.

l: death, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Death comes after life, and those who die remain behind a barrier until the day when they are raised.

l: the Day of Resurrection, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: On the Day of Resurrection people are raised again, deeds are weighed, and people are judged according to the weight of their scales.

l: water, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Allah sends water down from the sky in measure and gives it lodging in the earth, while being able to withdraw it. Water is also associated with the refuge given to the son of Mary and his mother.

l: earth, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Allah creates man from a product of wet earth and asks who owns the earth and whoever is in it. People answer that it belongs to Allah.

l: ship, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Allah commands Noah to make the ship under His eyes and inspiration. Noah and those with him are saved aboard it, and he asks Allah for a blessed landing-place.

l: Noah, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Noah calls his folk to serve Allah alone, but they deny him. Allah tells him to make the ship, saves him and those with him, and Noah asks for help because his people deny him.

l: Noah's folk, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Noah's folk reject his call and say he is only a mortal like them, or a man in whom there is madness. They are overtaken by the flood and destroyed.

l: the chieftains of Noah's folk, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: The chieftains of Noah's folk disbelieve, reject Noah, and claim that he seeks superiority over them. They say Allah would have sent angels if He had willed.

l: the flood, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: The flood occurs when the oven gushes water, and those who have done wrong are drowned.

l: messengers, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Allah sends messengers one after another to nations, but those nations deny them, so Allah causes them to follow one another to disaster and makes them bywords. The messengers are told to eat good things and do right.

l: Moses, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Moses is sent with Aaron and Allah's tokens and a clear warrant to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Allah gives Moses the Scripture so that people might go aright.

l: Aaron, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Aaron is sent with Moses, Allah's tokens, and a clear warrant to Pharaoh and his chiefs.

l: Pharaoh, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Pharaoh and his chiefs scorn Moses and Aaron, act despotically, and reject them as mortals like themselves. They are among those who are destroyed.

l: the Scripture, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Allah gives Moses the Scripture so that people might go aright.

l: the son of Mary, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: The son of Mary and his mother are made a portent and are given refuge on a height with flocks and watersprings.

l: the religion, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Allah says that the religion is one religion and that He is the Lord, commanding people to keep their duty to Him. Mankind breaks it into sects.

l: sects, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Mankind breaks the religion into sects, with each group rejoicing in what it has.

l: the Hereafter, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: The disbelieving chieftains deny the meeting of the Hereafter, and those who do not believe in it are astray from the path.

l: the revelations of the Lord, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: The believers believe in the revelations of their Lord and do not ascribe partners to Him. The disbelievers hear the revelations recited but turn back in scorn and deny them.

l: punishment, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Allah grasps luxurious people with punishment, but they do not humble themselves or pray. When extreme punishment is opened for them, they become aghast.

l: the seven heavens, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Allah is described as the Lord of the seven heavens.

l: the Tremendous Throne, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Allah is described as the Lord of the Tremendous Throne and as having dominion over all things.

l: Muhammad, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Muhammad is summoned to a straight path and is told to repel evil with what is better. He is instructed to seek refuge in Allah from the suggestions and presence of the evil ones.

l: the trumpet, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: When the trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship among people that day, and they will not ask one another.

l: the scales, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Those whose scales are heavy are successful, while those whose scales are light lose their souls and abide in hell.

l: hell, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Those with light scales lose their souls and abide in hell, where the fire burns their faces.

l: the fire, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: The fire burns the faces of those in hell, who are glum therein.

l: the steadfast slaves of Allah, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: The steadfast slaves of Allah believe, ask forgiveness and mercy, and are mocked by others. Allah rewards them for their steadfastness, and they are triumphant.

l: the disbelievers, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: The disbelievers reject messengers, deny resurrection, turn away from the revelations, and do not succeed. They face judgment, punishment, hell, and the fire.

l: the Truth, The Believers (Al-Muminoon), Surah 23: The Believers (Al-Muminoon)
s: Allah brings the Truth, but many are haters of it and reject it. The Truth is described as the message that should guide people to the straight path.

l: Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Surah 26 concerns revelation, Muhammad, and the warnings delivered through the stories of Moses, Abraham, Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, and Shu'eyb. Moses confronts Pharaoh, his wizards believe, the Children of Israel escape, and the sea parts before Pharaoh's people are drowned. Abraham rejects idols, while the peoples of Noah, A'ad, Thamud, Lot, and Midian deny their messengers and receive punishment. The unit affirms Allah's power, mercy, judgment, resurrection, and revelation, and concludes by distinguishing false poets from believers who do good works and remember Allah.

l: Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: It is revealed at Mecca and presents warnings, prophetic stories, signs, punishments, and teachings about revelation, faith, worship, judgment, and poetry.

l: Allah, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Allah is described as the Lord of the Worlds, the Mighty, the Merciful, the Creator, Guide, Provider, Healer, Giver of life, Forgiver, Judge, Hearer, and Knower.

l: Muhammad, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Muhammad is warned not to torment himself because people do not believe, and he is commanded to warn his near kindred, show kindness to believers, trust in Allah, and remain innocent of disobedience.

l: Moses, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Moses is sent to Pharaoh's folk with signs and Aaron, confronts Pharaoh, defeats the wizards' display, leads the Children of Israel away by night, and is guided when the two hosts meet.

l: Aaron, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Aaron is sent with Moses to Pharaoh's folk and is named as the Lord's servant and messenger alongside Moses.

l: Pharaoh, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Pharaoh questions Moses, claims authority, threatens him and the wizards who believe, gathers wizards to oppose him, and pursues Moses and the Children of Israel before being drowned.

l: Children of Israel, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The Children of Israel are enslaved by Pharaoh, are ordered to be released, leave by night with Moses, and are saved when the sea parts.

l: Egyptians (Pharaoh's folk), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Pharaoh's folk are called to ward off evil but reject the message, oppose Moses, pursue the Children of Israel, and are drowned.

l: Moses' wizards, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Moses' wizards throw down their cords and staves, but Moses' staff swallows their false display. They then fall prostrate, believe in the Lord of the Worlds, and face Pharaoh's threats.

l: Abraham, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Abraham asks his father and folk what they worship, rejects their idols, declares the Lord of the Worlds his only allegiance, and prays for wisdom, righteousness, forgiveness, and a good report.

l: Abraham's folk, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Abraham's folk worship idols because they found their fathers doing so and do not claim that the idols hear, benefit, or harm them.

l: idols, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The idols are worshipped by Abraham's folk, but Abraham declares them enemies and denies that they can hear, benefit, or harm.

l: Garden of Delight, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The Garden of Delight is among the inheritances Abraham asks for, and it is brought near for those who ward off evil.

l: hell, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Hell appears plainly to the erring, and those who worshipped instead of Allah are hurled into it with the seducers and the hosts of Iblis.

l: Noah, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Noah calls his folk to duty, obedience, and belief, refuses to repel believers, asks Allah for judgment between them, and is saved with the believers in the laden ship.

l: Noah's folk, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Noah's folk deny the messengers, reject Noah because lowly people follow him, threaten to stone him, and are drowned after Noah and those with him are saved.

l: believers, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Believers are defended by the prophets, saved with Noah and Moses in their respective trials, and are described as those who follow, do good works, remember Allah, and are not to be repelled.

l: the messengers of Allah, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The messengers repeatedly call their peoples to ward off evil, obey Allah, and obey them, while asking no wage except from the Lord of the Worlds.

l: the tribe of A'ad, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The tribe of A'ad denies the messengers, rejects Hud's warning, calls it an old fable, and is destroyed.

l: Hud, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Hud calls the tribe of A'ad to duty and obedience, reminds them of Allah's blessings of cattle, sons, gardens, and watersprings, and warns them of an awful day.

l: the tribe of Thamud, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The tribe of Thamud rejects Salih, demands a token, hamstrings the she-camel, becomes penitent, and receives retribution.

l: Salih, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Salih calls the tribe of Thamud to duty and obedience, gives the she-camel as a sign with an appointed drinking arrangement, and warns them not to harm it.

l: she-camel (Salih's sign), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The she-camel is given as a sign and has a right to drink at the well on an appointed day. The tribe of Thamud hamstrings it, after which retribution comes upon them.

l: the folk of Lot, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The folk of Lot deny the messengers, pursue conduct Lot hates, threaten to expel him, and are destroyed after rejecting his warning.

l: Lot, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Lot calls his folk to duty and obedience, condemns their conduct, declares his hatred of it, and prays to be saved with his household.

l: Lot's household, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Lot's household is saved with him, except for an old woman among those who stayed behind.

l: the dwellers in the wood of Midian, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The dwellers in the wood deny the messengers, reject Shu'eyb, demand that fragments of heaven fall upon them, and receive the punishment of the day of gloom.

l: Shu'eyb, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Shu'eyb calls the dwellers in the wood to duty, obedience, full measure, true weighing, justice, and avoidance of corruption, while asking no wage.

l: the True Spirit, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The True Spirit brings down the revelation upon Muhammad's heart so that he may be one of the warners.

l: the guilty, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The guilty do not believe in the revelation until they see the painful doom, and the revelation is made to traverse their hearts.

l: the devils, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The devils do not bring down the revelation and are banished from hearing. They descend upon every sinful, false one, who listens eagerly while most of them are liars.

l: the poets, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The erring follow the poets, who stray through every valley and say what they do not do, except for those who believe, do good works, remember Allah, and vindicate themselves after being wronged.

l: the believers who do good works, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: They are excepted from the condemnation of the poets because they believe, do good works, remember Allah much, and vindicate themselves after being wronged.

l: the earth, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The earth displays many fruitful kinds, which is identified as a sign, though most people are not believers.

l: the heavens, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The heavens are part of the Lord of the Worlds' dominion, and Moses identifies the Lord as the Lord of the heavens and the earth and all between them.

l: the sea, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The sea parts when Moses strikes it with his staff, with each part becoming like a vast mountain, allowing Moses and those with him to escape.

l: Moses' staff, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Moses' staff becomes a manifest serpent, swallows what the wizards falsely display, and parts the sea when Moses strikes it.

l: wizards' cords and staves, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The wizards throw down their cords and staves, which create a false display that is swallowed by Moses' staff.

l: gardens, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Gardens are among Allah's signs and blessings, among the possessions taken from Pharaoh's people and mentioned in the warnings to A'ad, Thamud, and others.

l: watersprings, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Watersprings are among Allah's blessings and are mentioned as possessions of Pharaoh's people, A'ad, Thamud, and Abraham's requested Garden of Delight.

l: the laden ship, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The laden ship carries Noah and those with him, who are saved in it before the others are drowned.

l: the flood of Noah, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The flood of Noah is represented by the drowning of Noah's folk after Noah and those with him are saved in the laden ship.

l: the Exodus from Egypt, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The Exodus from Egypt begins when Moses is inspired to take Allah's servants away by night, while Pharaoh sends summoners and pursues them.

l: the parting of the sea, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The parting of the sea saves Moses and those with him and brings Pharaoh's forces near before the others are drowned.

l: the punishment of A'ad, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The punishment of A'ad is the destruction that follows their denial of Hud and their rejection of the warning.

l: the punishment of Thamud, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The punishment of Thamud comes after they hamstring the she-camel, and they are destroyed.

l: the punishment of Lot's people, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The punishment of Lot's people includes their destruction and a rain described as dreadful after Lot and most of his household are saved.

l: the day of gloom, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The day of gloom brings the retribution of an awful day upon the dwellers in the wood after they deny Shu'eyb.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The Day of Judgment is when wealth and sons do not avail anyone except one who brings a whole heart, and when Abraham hopes for forgiveness of his sin.

l: resurrection, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Resurrection is presented as the day when people are raised, when wealth and sons cannot help, and when the erring face hell.

l: the painful doom, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The painful doom comes suddenly to those who refuse belief, after which they ask whether they will be reprieved.

l: revelation, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: The revelation comes from the Lord of the Worlds through the True Spirit upon Muhammad's heart in plain Arabic speech and is found in the Scriptures of earlier peoples.

l: prophethood and warning, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Prophethood and warning are shown through messengers who call their peoples to duty, obedience, faith, justice, and repentance while asking no worldly wage.

l: faith, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Faith is affirmed by the wizards, the believers, and those who trust Allah, while most of the peoples described reject it despite witnessing signs.

l: worship, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Worship belongs to Allah, while Abraham rejects the worship of idols and the condemned are questioned about what they worshipped instead of Allah.

l: magic, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Magic is claimed by Pharaoh to be Moses' means of driving people from their land, but Moses' sign defeats the wizards' display and the wizards come to believe.

l: repentance and forgiveness, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Abraham asks forgiveness for himself and his father, the wizards hope Allah will forgive their sins, and repentance follows the hamstringing of the she-camel.

l: judgment, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Judgment belongs to Allah, who judges between Noah and his folk, brings the Garden near to those who ward off evil, and punishes the erring.

l: justice and fair dealing, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Shu'eyb commands full measure, true weighing, and no wronging of mankind in their goods.

l: corruption, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Corruption is condemned in the warnings to those who spread it in the earth and do not reform, and in the commands not to make mischief.

l: poetry, Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa), Surah 26: The Poets (Ash-Shu'araa)
s: Poetry is criticized when poets stray, say what they do not do, and are followed by the erring, while believing poets who do good works and remember Allah are excepted.

l: Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas) recounts Moses’ life, from his infancy and escape from Pharaoh to his call as a messenger and confrontation with Pharaoh. It describes Pharaoh’s oppression, the destruction of Pharaoh and his hosts through drowning in the sea, and Allah’s guidance and warnings to Muhammad and the people. The unit also tells of Korah’s wealth, arrogance, and swallowing by the earth, and contrasts worldly comfort with the Hereafter. It affirms Allah’s sole authority, the truth of the Qur'an, accountability on the Day of Resurrection, and the consequences of corruption.

l: Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas) narrates the story of Moses and Pharaoh, gives warnings about disbelief and corruption, and affirms Allah’s authority and the reality of the Hereafter.

l: Allah, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: Allah guides whom He wills, forgives Moses, gives him wisdom and knowledge, supports him and Aaron, and destroys wrongdoers. Allah alone has command, all praise, and the knowledge of what people conceal and reveal.

l: Moses, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: Moses is born under Pharaoh’s oppression, placed in the river, raised in Pharaoh’s household, and later flees after killing a man. He reaches Midian, helps the two women, marries into their household, and is then called by Allah and sent with signs to Pharaoh.

l: Pharaoh, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: Pharaoh exalts himself, divides the people into castes, kills their sons, and spares their women. He rejects Moses, claims to know no god other than himself, and is seized and abandoned to the sea.

l: Muhammad, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: Muhammad is told that he was not present at Moses’ earlier events but received knowledge of them as a mercy from his Lord. He is instructed to warn people, call them to Allah, and not be diverted from the revelations.

l: Korah, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: Korah is from Moses’ folk and oppresses them after receiving immense treasure. He exults in his wealth, refuses admonition, and is swallowed by the earth together with his dwelling-place.

l: the mother of Moses, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The mother of Moses is inspired to nurse him and cast him into the river when she fears for him. Allah strengthens her heart, returns Moses to her, and comforts her by fulfilling His promise.

l: the two women of Midian, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The two women of Midian keep back their flocks while shepherds water theirs because their father is old. Moses waters their flock, and one of them later recommends that their father hire him as a strong and trustworthy worker.

l: Pharaoh's hosts, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: Pharaoh's hosts support him in oppression and rejection of Moses. Allah seizes them with Pharaoh and abandons them to the sea, making them patterns that invite unto the Fire.

l: Moses' folk, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: Moses' folk include those whom Korah oppresses and those who warn him not to exult or seek corruption. After Korah is swallowed, some recognize that Allah enlarges and restricts provision as He wills.

l: the Israelites, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The Israelites are represented in this unit as the oppressed tribe among Pharaoh’s people whose sons were killed and women spared. Allah desires to favour the oppressed, make them inheritors, and establish them in the earth.

l: believers, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: Believers include those who trust Allah’s revelations, repent, do right, remain steadfast, repel evil with good, and spend from what Allah provides. They are promised success and reward.

l: the people of the Scripture, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The people of the Scripture who received Scripture before the Qur'an believe in it when it is recited and say that it is truth from their Lord. They are given their reward twice for steadfastness and good conduct.

l: the messengers, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The messengers are questioned about the answers they received from their peoples on the Day of Resurrection. Allah raises messengers before destroying townships so that the people have warning.

l: the communities, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The communities that are thankless for their means of livelihood may be destroyed, leaving their dwellings mostly uninhabited. Allah does not destroy communities until a messenger has recited revelations to them and they have become wrongdoers.

l: Midian, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: Midian is where Moses turns after fleeing Pharaoh and where he finds the two women at the water. He helps them, is welcomed by their father, and remains there for a term.

l: the city, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The city is where Moses enters at a time when its people are careless and finds two men fighting. After the killing and the threat against him become known, Moses flees from the city.

l: the sea, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The sea is where Allah abandons Pharaoh and his hosts after seizing them. Their drowning becomes an example and a consequence for evil-doers.

l: the earth, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The earth is the place where Pharaoh exalts himself and seeks corruption, and it swallows Korah and his dwelling-place by Allah’s command.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The Hereafter is better and more lasting than the comfort and ornament of the world. Its abode is assigned to those who do not seek oppression or corruption in the earth.

l: the world, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The world offers temporary comfort and ornament, while what Allah has is better and more lasting. People who desire the worldly life admire Korah’s wealth, but those given knowledge prefer Allah’s reward.

l: the Scripture, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The Scripture is given as clear testimonies, guidance, and mercy, and it reaches people so that they may take heed. Moses receives the Scripture after the destruction of earlier generations.

l: the Qur'an, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The Qur'an is given to Muhammad as a law and a mercy from his Lord. Muhammad is told to call people to his Lord and not help the disbelievers.

l: the Truth, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The Truth comes from Allah, but some people reject it and ask why Muhammad was not given the like of what was given to Moses. The Truth is affirmed as belonging to Allah, while invented claims fail.

l: guidance, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: Guidance comes from Allah, and no one can guide whom Allah has not chosen to guide. Following lust without guidance is described as the farthest error.

l: the Fire, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: Pharaoh and his followers are made patterns that invite unto the Fire. They will not be helped on the Day of Resurrection.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: On the Day of Resurrection, people are called to account about their alleged partners and their answers to the messengers. The disbelievers’ invented claims fail, while repentant believers who do right may be successful.

l: the destruction of Pharaoh and his hosts, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The destruction of Pharaoh and his hosts occurs when Allah seizes them and abandons them to the sea. They become patterns inviting unto the Fire and are followed by a curse in this world.

l: the drowning in the sea, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The drowning in the sea is the fate of Pharaoh and his hosts after their haughtiness and rejection of Moses. It demonstrates the consequence awaiting evil-doers.

l: the swallowing of Korah, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: The swallowing of Korah occurs when Allah causes the earth to swallow Korah and his dwelling-place. Korah has no host to help him against Allah and cannot save himself.

l: Korah's treasure, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: Korah's treasure is so abundant that its stores would burden a troop of mighty men. Its possession leads Korah to exult and causes worldly-minded people to envy him.

l: corruption, Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas), Surah 28: The Stories (Al-Qasas)
s: Corruption is associated with Pharaoh, who works corruption through oppression, and with Korah, who is warned not to seek it in the earth. Allah does not love corrupters, and the Hereafter belongs to those who avoid oppression and corruption.

l: Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: This unit concerns Allah’s sovereignty, knowledge, provision, judgment, and power over the heavens and earth. It recounts what Allah gave David and Solomon, the ingratitude and scattering of Sheba, and the deception of Satan. It describes the claims and punishment of disbelievers, the reward of believers, and Muhammad’s mission as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. It affirms the coming Hour, resurrection, judgment, the truth of Allah’s revelations, and the failure of falsehood.

l: Allah, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: Allah possesses and praises everything in the heavens and the earth, knows all hidden and manifest things, and will judge and reward people according to their belief and deeds. He gives provision, replaces what is spent for good, sends messengers and revelations, and is the Mighty, Wise, Merciful, Forgiving, and Best of Providers.

l: Muhammad, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: Muhammad is sent to all mankind as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. He is told to proclaim Allah’s truth, the coming promise, the resurrection, and his dependence on Allah’s revelation.

l: David, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: David was given grace from Allah, and the hills and birds echoed his praise. Allah made iron supple for him and instructed him to make coats of mail properly.

l: Solomon, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: Solomon was given the wind, a fountain of copper, and jinn who worked for him by Allah’s permission. The jinn made for him what he willed, while those who deviated from Allah’s command tasted the punishment of flaming Fire.

l: Satan, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: Satan found his calculation concerning the people true because they followed him, except for a group of true believers. He had no authority over them except that Allah would distinguish those who believe in the Hereafter from those who doubt.

l: Sheba, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: Sheba had a sign in its dwelling-place: two gardens with provision and a gracious land. Because its people were froward and ungrateful, Allah sent the flood of 'Iram, replaced their gardens with inferior ones, and scattered them.

l: the jinn, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: Some jinn worked for Solomon by permission of his Lord and made what he willed. They did not know the Unseen, as shown when they continued their toil after Solomon’s death until his staff was gnawed away.

l: the angels, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: The angels will deny that those who worshipped them were worshipping them. They will declare Allah alone their Guardian and say that the people worshipped the jinn.

l: believers, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: Believers who do good works receive pardon, rich provision, and multiplied reward, and they dwell securely in lofty halls. A group of true believers were not led by Satan.

l: disbelievers, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: Disbelievers deny the Hour, resurrection, the Qur'an, and Allah’s revelations, and they challenge the messengers. They will face torment, the doom of the Fire, remorse, and carcans on their necks.

l: mankind, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: Muhammad is sent as a warner and bringer of good tidings to all mankind, though most of mankind do not know. Mankind is warned that wealth and children do not bring people near to Allah.

l: the Qur'an, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: The Qur'an is rejected by disbelievers along with what came before it, though its truth is affirmed in the unit. Those who disbelieve call it invented falsehood or magic.

l: Allah's revelations, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: Allah's revelations are described as truth that leads to the path of the Mighty, the Owner of Praise. Those who strive against them in challenge will be brought to the doom.

l: the Hour, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: The Hour will surely come, and not even an atom’s weight escapes Allah’s knowledge. Disbelievers deny that it will come, but they cannot postpone or hasten it.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: Belief in the Hereafter distinguishes true believers from those in doubt. Disbelievers who deny it are in torment and far error.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: On the appointed day, Allah will gather all people, judge between them with truth, question the angels about those who worshipped them, and tell wrongdoers to taste the doom of the Fire.

l: the Fire, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: The Fire is a punishment for those among the jinn who deviate from Allah’s command and for those who deny the truth. Those who do wrong will be told to taste its doom.

l: the earth, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: Allah knows what enters the earth and what comes forth from it. He can make the earth swallow people, and everything in it belongs to Him.

l: falsehood, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: Falsehood will not show its face or return when the truth comes. Disbelievers describe the truth as invented falsehood or mere magic.

l: faith, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: Faith is affirmed through belief in Allah, the Hereafter, and doing good works. Faith cannot be reached after people are seized by terror and separated from what they desire.

l: punishment, Surah 34: Sheba (Saba), Surah 34: Sheba (Saba)
s: Punishment comes to those who challenge Allah’s revelations, disbelieve, are ungrateful, or deviate from His command. It includes painful doom, flaming Fire, the doom of the Fire, and carcans on the necks of disbelievers.

l: Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen) concerns Ya Sin, the revelation of the Qur'an, warnings to humanity, and signs of Allah's power. It describes the people of the city rejecting the messengers, while a man from the city urges them to follow those who ask no fee. It presents signs in the earth, night, sun, moon, living creatures, and human creation, and describes the resurrection, the trumpet blast, paradise, hell, and the Day of Judgment. It concludes that Allah's command brings things into being and that all will be brought back to Him.

l: Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen) contains a warning, reminders of Allah's signs, and descriptions of the resurrection, paradise, hell, and the Day of Judgment.

l: Ya Sin, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: Ya Sin is addressed as one of those sent on the straight path with a revelation from the Mighty, the Merciful.

l: Allah, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: Allah sends messengers, gives signs, revives the dead, records deeds, and will bring all people before Him. His command is that when He intends a thing, He says to it, 'Be!' and it is.

l: Muhammad, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: Muhammad is told that he is one of those sent and that he has not been taught poetry, but a Reminder and a Lecture making plain.

l: Qur'an, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: The Qur'an is described as wise and as a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful.

l: the Beneficent, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: The Beneficent is feared in secret, promises what the messengers spoke, and grants peace to those who merit paradise.

l: the Lord, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: The Lord is the one to whom people will be brought back. The man from the city declares belief in his Lord, and the Lord pardons him and makes him one of the honoured ones.

l: the people of the city, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: The people of the city reject the messengers, call them liars, threaten to stone them, and are destroyed by one Shout.

l: the city, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: The city is where the messengers arrive and where a man comes running from its uttermost part to urge the people to follow them.

l: the messengers, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: The messengers are sent to the people of the city and state that they have been sent to them. They ask for no fee and are rightly guided, but the people mock and reject them.

l: the man from the city, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: The man from the city comes running from its uttermost part and urges his people to follow the messengers. He declares belief in his Lord, is told to enter paradise, and wishes that his people knew of his pardon and honour.

l: the believers, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: The believers are addressed by those who disbelieve in a dispute about feeding those whom Allah could feed if He willed.

l: the disbelievers, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: The disbelievers do not believe despite warnings, mock the messengers, reject signs, dispute the promise, and are threatened with hell. Their mouths will be sealed, while their hands and feet testify to what they earned.

l: humanity, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: Humanity is warned to worship Allah rather than the devil and is reminded of creation, death, resurrection, and accountability for deeds.

l: the devil, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: The devil is described as an open foe of the sons of Adam and as one who has led a great multitude astray.

l: paradise, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: Paradise is entered by the honoured man from the city and is the reward of those who merit it. Its inhabitants recline in pleasant shade, have fruit and whatever they ask, and receive peace from a Merciful Lord.

l: hell, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: Hell is the promised destination of those who follow the devil and disbelieve. They are told to burn therein for their disbelief.

l: the resurrection, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: The resurrection is described when the dead are raised from their graves and brought together before Allah. The dead earth being revived is given as a sign of this power.

l: the trumpet blast, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: The trumpet blast is one Shout that causes people to come from their graves and be brought together before Allah. Another Shout destroys the people of the city and another surprises people while they dispute.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: On the Day of Judgment, no soul is wronged, each is requited for what it did, and hands and feet testify to deeds.

l: the straight path, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: The straight path is the path on which Ya Sin is sent and the right path associated with worshipping Allah rather than the devil.

l: the earth, Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen), Surah 36: Yaseen (Yaseen)
s: The earth is presented as a sign when Allah revives its dead parts and brings forth grain, gardens, date-palms, grapes, and springs for people to eat and give thanks.

l: Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat), Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat), Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: The unit affirms that Allah is One, Lord of the heavens, earth, and all between them, and describes the Day of Judgment, the Day of Separation, resurrection, questioning, punishment, and reward. It contrasts idolaters and those who reject monotheism with believers and single-minded slaves of Allah, who receive provision and honor in the Gardens of delight. It recounts how Allah saved Noah, Abraham, Abraham's son, Moses, Aaron, Elias, Lot, and Jonah, and how Abraham's sacrifice was replaced with a tremendous victim. The unit also condemns the tree of Zaqqum and hell, and concludes with Allah's promise that His sent servants and host will be helped and victorious.

l: Allah, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat), Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: Allah is One and is Lord of the heavens, earth, all that is between them, and the sun's risings. He created creation, sent warners, saved His believing slaves, rewards the good, punishes the guilty, and is glorified above what is attributed to Him.

l: Noah, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat), Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: Noah prayed to Allah, whose hearing of the prayer was gracious. Allah saved Noah and his household from the great distress, made his seed survivors, and left peace for him among later peoples.

l: Abraham, Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat), Surah 37: Those drawn up in Ranks (As-Saaffaat)
s: Abraham came to his Lord with a whole heart and rejected worship of gods beside Allah. He confronted his people and their idols, was saved from their planned fire, and received tidings of a gentle son and Isaac.
